Modern.brandNameRationale: The dramaturg is the literary-and-context role formalized by Lessing at the Hamburg National Theatre in 1767 (Hamburgische Dramaturgie) — still the production's intellectual conscience. The brand puts the dramaturg on the marquee.
Modern.industrySummary: Modern producing theaters have been competing on celebrity casting and Broadway-aspirant programming. There is room for a company that puts the literary intelligence behind the season on the marquee.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Soho Rep (sohorep.org) holds the modern producing peer position. Playwrights Horizons (playwrightshorizons.org) plays the new-writing reference. Lincoln Center Theater (lct.org) sits in the institutional middle. We sit smaller and more curatorial.
Modern.positioningStatement: A modern producing theater curated around a guest dramaturg's argument.

targetAudience.primary: 30 to 55. Sees ten plays a year. Reads the program before the curtain. Subscribes to the literary magazines.

dos: Publish the dramaturg's argument before the season
Name the guest dramaturg on the marquee
Print the season program as an essay

Modern.logoDirection: A wordmark. The Dramaturg set in a calm modern serif, with a single underline beneath the word, suggesting the dramaturg's pencil mark on the script.

typography.primary: GT Sectra for the wordmark and the program
typography.rationale: Sectra carries the literary register. Söhne handles the ticketing.

Luxury.brandNameRationale: Theatre Royal, Drury Lane (London, 1663 patent) and David Garrick — the actor-manager who ran it 1747–1776 and naturalized Shakespeare on the modern stage. The pair places the brand in the English actor-manager lineage. Drury and Garrick are historical and geographic references, not active marks.
Luxury.industrySummary: Top-end producing theater has been moving toward subscription packages and corporate hospitality. There is space for a producing house anchored in the English actor-manager tradition — a named principal company, flagship Shakespeare, a season subscription that means something.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: Royal Shakespeare Company (rsc.org.uk) holds the institutional reference. National Theatre (nationaltheatre.org.uk) plays the producing peer. Donmar Warehouse (donmarwarehouse.com) sits in the prestige middle. We sit smaller and more actor-led.
Luxury.positioningStatement: A luxury producing house anchored in the English actor-manager tradition.

targetAudience.primary: 45 to 75. Subscribes to two opera houses. Sees the principal actor every season. Donates to the building fund.
behaviors: Holds the same box for years

Luxury.logoDirection: A serif wordmark. Drury & Garrick set in a high-contrast classical face, with a single hand-drawn proscenium-arch hallmark, used in gold foil on the season subscription card.

typography.primary: Caslon for the wordmark and printed program
typography.secondary: Söhne for the few digital surfaces
typography.rationale: Caslon carries the English playbill heritage. Söhne handles the seat-map confirmation.

Minimal.tagline: One place. One time. One action.
Minimal.brandNameRationale: The three Aristotelian unities (time, place, action) — the Renaissance reading of Aristotle's Poetics that governed French neoclassical drama (Racine, Corneille). The brand is the constraint.
Minimal.industrySummary: Black-box theater has been programming festivals of short pieces and crossover work. There is room for a minimal company that holds the line on the unities — one play at a time, one set, one continuous timeframe.
Minimal.competitorLandscape: The Wooster Group (thewoostergroup.org) plays the experimental minimalist peer. Big Dance Theater (bigdancetheater.org) sits in the formal-constraint middle. We sit further out — the unities are the brand.
Minimal.positioningStatement: A theater company whose programming is the formal constraint.

targetAudience.primary: Adults who want one play, one set, one continuous evening. They want the form to do the work.

dos: State the time, place, and action

Minimal.logoDirection: A wordmark only. Unities in a single-weight grotesk, set wide. The favicon is a single small dot — the unity of place reduced to a point.

typography.rationale: One face. The form is the brand.

Corporate.brandNameRationale: The repertory system — the rotating-program model adopted by the Moscow Art Theatre, the Berliner Ensemble, and Britain's regional reps (Birmingham Rep, founded 1913). The definite article + Company suffix places the brand in the institutional producing tradition.
Corporate.industrySummary: Regional producing theater has been competing for civic funding and corporate hospitality. There is space for an institution that operates on the repertory model — resident company, rotating season, standing corporate boxes.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Steppenwolf Theatre Company (steppenwolf.org) holds the resident-ensemble reference. Manhattan Theatre Club (manhattantheatreclub.com) plays the institutional peer. Roundabout Theatre Company (roundabouttheatre.org) sits in the subscription middle. We sit closer to Steppenwolf in posture.
Corporate.positioningStatement: A resident company on a rotating-season repertory model, with civic and corporate hospitality.

targetAudience.primary: Corporate hospitality buyers, civic foundation officers, and season subscribers at companies and institutions with annual cultural-giving budgets.

dos: Speak to the subscriber, not the single ticket

Corporate.logoDirection: A wordmark with a small geometric mark to the left. The mark is a thin proscenium arch reduced to three strokes. Reads cleanly on a season subscription card, a corporate-box pass, and an email signature.

typography.primary: Inter for the website and ticketing
typography.secondary: Source Serif Pro for the printed season program
typography.rationale: Inter scales clean. The serif carries the printed season program.

Creative.tagline: Three playwrights. Three days. One verdict.
Creative.brandNameRationale: The City Dionysia — the Athenian festival (6th c. BC) where Aeschylus, Sophocles, and Euripides competed and Western tragedy was invented; the ancestor of every festival from Avignon to Edinburgh. The single word places the brand in the festival lineage.
Creative.industrySummary: Theater festivals have been chasing celebrity directors and Hollywood programming. There is room for a creative festival structured as a competition — three playwrights, three days, an audience verdict.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Edinburgh International Festival (eif.co.uk) holds the festival reference. Under the Radar (publictheater.org) plays the new-work festival peer. Avignon Festival (festival-avignon.com) sits in the European middle. We sit smaller and more competitive — the verdict is the form.
Creative.positioningStatement: A theater festival structured as a competition.

targetAudience.primary: 30 to 60. Buys a festival pass. Sees three plays in three days. Votes at the end.
behaviors: Reads about the playwrights in advance

dos: Publish the rules of the verdict

Creative.logoDirection: A wordmark. Dionysia set in a punchy display serif, with a single hand-drawn laurel-wreath sprig as the hallmark, used on the festival pass and the printed ballot.

typography.primary: GT Sectra for the wordmark and printed material
typography.rationale: Sectra carries the editorial register of the festival. Söhne handles the booking.
